evidence.pali: 207 . ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, evaṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati kāmavitakko. So evaṃ pajānāmi – ‘uppanno kho me ayaṃ kāmavitakko. So ca kho attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattaniko’ anibbānasaṃvattaniko’’ti (?) . ‘Attabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘parabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘ubhayabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattaniko’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, uppannuppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ pajahameva atītakālikakiriyāpadāniyeva vinodameva atītakālikakiriyāpadāniyeva byantameva byanteva (sī. syā. pī.) naṃ akāsiṃ.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 207. “诸比丘，我如是不放逸、热忱、专心致志而住时，生起了欲寻。我这样了知：‘我这欲寻已生起。它既导致恼害自己，也导致恼害他人，还导致恼害双方；它障碍智慧，属于恼害的一方，不导向涅槃。’诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害自己’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害他人’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害双方’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它障碍智慧，属于恼害的一方，不导向涅槃’时，它就消失了。诸比丘，我就是这样，对每一个生起的欲寻，都予以舍断、去除、灭尽。”
evidence.english: 207. “Monks, as I was dwelling thus—heedful, ardent, and resolute—a thought of sensual desire arose in me. I understood it thus: ‘This thought of sensual desire has arisen in me. It leads to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; it obstructs wisdom, is on the side of distress, and does not lead to Nibbāna.’ As I reflected, ‘It leads to my own affliction,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It leads to the affliction of others,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It leads to the affliction of both,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It obstructs wisdom, is on the side of distress, and does not lead to Nibbāna,’ it subsided in me. Monks, I would abandon, dispel, and make an end of each thought of sensual desire as it arose.

entries.pali: Ayaṃ ñāṇasaṃvaro nāma. ‘‘Khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.24; a. ni. 4.114; 6.58) ayaṃ khantisaṃvaro . ‘‘Uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāsetī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.26; a. ni. 4.114; 6.58) ayaṃ vīriyasaṃvaro . Sabbopi cāyaṃ saṃvaro yathāsakaṃ saṃvaritabbānaṃ vinetabbānañca kāyaduccaritādīnaṃ saṃvaraṇato saṃvaro, vinayanato vinayoti vuccati. Evaṃ tāva ‘saṃvaravinayo’ pañcadhā bhijjatīti veditabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 此名为智防护。“能忍受寒热”（《中部》1.24；《增支部》4.114；6.58），此为忍耐防护。“不容受已生起的欲寻”（《中部》1.26；《增支部》4.114；6.58），此为精进防护。并且，所有此等防护，因其防护各自应防护及应调伏的身恶行等，故称为“防护”；因其调伏，故称为“调伏”。如是，当知“防护调伏”分为五种。
entries.english: This is called the restraint of knowledge. “He is able to endure cold and heat” (Ma. Ni. 1.24; etc.)—this is the restraint of patience. “He does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual pleasure” (Ma. Ni. 1.26; etc.)—this is the restraint of energy. And all this restraint is called ‘restraint’ (saṃvara) because of its restraining of bodily misconduct and so on, which are to be restrained and disciplined; and it is called ‘discipline’ (vinaya) because of its disciplining. Thus, for now, it should be understood that the ‘discipline of restraint’ is divided fivefold.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: 181 . Tatiyachakke kāmo ti dve kāmā – vatthukāmo ca kilesakāmo ca. Tattha kilesakāmaṃ sandhāya kāmapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu kāmadhātu, kāmavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vatthukāmaṃ sandhāya kāmoyeva dhātu kāmadhātu, kāmāvacaradhammānametaṃ nāmaṃ. Byāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu byāpādadhātu, byāpādavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Byāpādova dhātu byāpādadhātu, dasaāghātavatthukassa paṭighassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vihiṃsā paṭisaṃyuttā dhātu vihiṃsādhātu, vihiṃsāvitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vihiṃsāyeva dhātu vihiṃsādhātu, parasattavihesanassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Ayaṃ pana heṭṭhā anāgatattā evaṃ atthādivibhāgato veditabbā – vihiṃsanti etāya satte, vihiṃsanaṃ vā etaṃ sattānanti vihiṃsā. Sā viheṭhanalakkhaṇā, karuṇāpaṭipakkhalakkhaṇā vā; parasantāne ubbegajananarasā, sakasantāne karuṇāviddhaṃsanarasā vā; dukkhāyatanapaccupaṭṭhānā; paṭighapadaṭṭhānāti veditabbā. Nekkhammaṃ vuccati lobhā nikkhantattā alobho, nīvaraṇehi nikkhantattā paṭhamajjhānaṃ, sabbākusalehi nikkhantattā sabbakusalaṃ. Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu nekkhammadhātu, nekkhammavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Nekkhammameva dhātu nekkhammadhātu, sabbassāpi kusalassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu abyāpādadhātu, abyāpādavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Abyāpādova dhātu abyāpādadhātu, mettāyetaṃ nāmaṃ. Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu avihiṃsādhātu, avihiṃsā vitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Avihiṃsāva dhātu avihiṃsādhātu, karuṇāyetaṃ nāmaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 181. 于第三组六界中，欲有两种：事欲(vatthukāma)与烦恼欲(kilesakāma)。其中，与烦恼欲相应的界为欲界，此是欲寻之名。与事欲相应者，欲本身即是界，为欲界，此是欲界诸法之名。与瞋相应的界为瞋界，此是瞋寻之名。瞋本身即是界，为瞋界，此是十愤恨事之名。与害相应的界为害界，此是害寻之名。害本身即是界，为害界，此是恼害他有情之名。此“害”因前文未述，故当从义理等方面作此分别：以其伤害有情，或对有情的伤害，故为“害”。其特征为恼害，或与悲相反；作用为于他人生起怖畏，或于自身毁坏悲心；现起为苦的依处；近因为瞋，当如是了知。出离，因出离贪欲，故为无贪；因出离诸盖，故为初禅；因出离一切不善法，故为一切善法。与出离相应的界为出离界，此是出离寻之名。出离本身即是界，为出离界，此是一切善法之名。与无瞋相应的界为无瞋界，此是无瞋寻之名。无瞋本身即是界，为无瞋界，此是慈之名。与无害相应的界为无害界，此是无害寻之名。无害本身即是界，为无害界，此是悲之名。
entries.english: 181. In the third set of six, 'sensual desire' (kāma) refers to two kinds of sensual desire: sensual objects (vatthukāma) and defilement-sensual desire (kilesakāma). Herein, with reference to defilement-sensual desire, the element associated with sensual desire is the sensual-desire element (kāmadhātu); this is a name for sensual thought (kāmavitakka). With reference to sensual objects, the element that is simply sensual desire is the sensual-desire element; this is a name for phenomena of the sense-sphere (kāmāvacaradhammā). The element associated with ill will is the ill-will element (byāpādadhātu); this is a name for ill-will thought (byāpādavitakka). The element that is simply ill will is the ill-will element; this is a name for aversion (paṭigha) based on the ten grounds for anger (dasa āghātavatthu). The element associated with cruelty is the cruelty element (vihiṃsādhātu); this is a name for cruelty thought (vihiṃsāvitakka). The element that is simply cruelty is the cruelty element; this is a name for the tormenting of other beings (parasattavihesana). This, however, as it has not been mentioned before, should be understood by way of its division into meaning, and so forth: 'vihiṃsā' means that by which beings are harmed, or it is the harming of beings. It has the characteristic of injuring, or the characteristic of being the antithesis of compassion; its function is to generate agitation in the continuity of others, or to destroy compassion in one's own continuity; it manifests as a basis for suffering; and it has aversion (paṭigha) as its proximate cause. 'Renunciation' (nekkhamma) is said to be non-greed because of having departed from greed, the first jhāna because of having departed from the hindrances, and all that is wholesome because of having departed from all that is unwholesome. The element associated with renunciation is the renunciation element (nekkhammadhātu); this is a name for renunciation thought (nekkhammavitakka). The element that is simply renunciation is the renunciation element; this is a name for all that is wholesome (sabbakusala). The element associated with non-ill-will is the non-ill-will element (abyāpādadhātu); this is a name for non-ill-will thought (abyāpādavitakka). The element that is simply non-ill-will is the non-ill-will element; this is a name for loving-kindness (mettā). The element associated with non-cruelty is the non-cruelty element (avihiṃsādhātu); this is a name for non-cruelty thought (avihiṃsāvitakka). The element that is simply non-cruelty is the non-cruelty element; this is a name for compassion (karuṇā).

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Sammāsaṅkappa niddese kāmato nissaṭoti nekkhammasaṅkappo . Byāpādato nissaṭoti abyāpādasaṅkappo . Vihiṃsāya nissaṭoti avihiṃsāsaṅkappo . Tattha nekkhammavitakko kāmavitakkassa padaghātaṃ padacchedaṃ karonto uppajjati, abyāpādavitakko byāpādavitakkassa, avihiṃsāvitakko vihiṃsāvitakkassa. Nekkhammavitakko ca kāmavitakkassa paccanīko hutvā uppajjati, abyāpādaavihiṃsāvitakkā byāpādavihiṃsāvitakkānaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 在正思惟的解释中，‘离于欲’即出离寻，‘离于嗔’即无嗔寻，‘离于害’即无害寻。于此，出离寻生起时，截断、破除欲寻；无嗔寻截断嗔寻；无害寻截断害寻。出离寻作为欲寻的对治法而生起，无嗔寻与无害寻亦作为嗔寻与害寻的对立面而生起。
entries.english: In the exposition of right intention: The thought of renunciation is that which has emerged from sensual desire. The thought of non-ill-will is that which has emerged from ill-will. The thought of non-harming is that which has emerged from harm. Herein, the thought of renunciation arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of sensual desire; the thought of non-ill-will arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of ill-will; and the thought of non-harming arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of harm. The thought of renunciation arises as an opponent to the thought of sensual desire, and the thoughts of non-ill-will and non-harming arise as opponents to the thoughts of ill-will and harm.

entries.pali: 182 . Ubhayattha uppannopi abhijjhāsaṃyogena kammapathajananato anabhijjhākammapathabhindanato ca kāmavitakko ‘‘kammapathabhedo’’ ti vutto . Byāpādo panā ti byāpādavacanena byāpādavitakkaṃ dasseti. So hi byāpādadhātūti. Tathā vihiṃsāya vihiṃsādhātuyā ca byāpādavasena yathāsambhavaṃ pāṇātipātādivasena ca kammapathabhedo yojetabbo. Etthā ti dvīsu tikesu. Sabbakāmāvacarasabbakusalasaṅgāhakehi itare dve dve saṅgahetvā kathanaṃ sabbasaṅgāhikakathā. Etthā ti pana etasmiṃ chakketi vuccamāne kāmadhātuvacanena kāmāvacarānaṃ nekkhammadhātuādīnañca gahaṇaṃ āpajjati.
entries.chinese_simplified: 182. 欲寻（kāmavitakka）虽于两处生起，但因与贪欲（abhijjhā）相应而生起业道，及破坏无贪业道，故被称为‘破业道’。至于嗔恚（byāpāda），是以‘嗔恚’一词显示嗔恚寻（byāpādavitakka），而那即是嗔恚界。同样，于害（vihiṃsā）与害界，应随其可能，以嗔恚或杀生等方式连结于破业道。‘于此’是指于二种三法组中。通过提及能含摄一切欲界善法的法组，从而也含摄了其余两组，这样的说法是总摄一切之说。若说‘于此’是指于此六法组中，则以‘欲界’一词，会导致摄取了欲界法与出离界（nekkhammadhātu）等。
entries.english: 182. Even when arising in both ways, a thought of sensual desire is called 'a breach in the path of action' because it generates a path of action through its connection with covetousness and because it breaches the path of non-covetousness. As to 'ill will,' this indicates a thought of ill will by the term 'ill will.' For that is the element of ill will. Similarly, a breach in the path of action should be connected with cruelty and the element of cruelty by way of ill will and, as may be the case, by way of killing living beings and so on. Here, in the two triads, the statement is an all-inclusive one, made by including the other two members of each triad under the all-inclusive terms for all that pertains to the sensual sphere and all that is wholesome. But here, when this sixfold set is spoken of, the term 'element of sensuality' would entail the inclusion of things belonging to the sensual sphere and also of the element of renunciation and so on.

entries.pali: So ti kāmavitakkappavattiyā kāraṇabhūto subhanimitte ayonisomanasikāro. Tassā ti kāmavitakkassa. Gataṃ gamanaṃ pavatti, tassa upāyoti gatamaggo .
entries.chinese_simplified: “彼”，即于净相(subhanimitta)不如理作意，此是欲寻转起之因。“彼”，即彼欲寻。“所行”，即行、转起，其方便即“所行道”。
entries.english: "That" is unwise attention to an attractive sign, which is the cause for the arising of sensual thoughts. "Of that" means of the sensual thought. "Gone" means going, occurrence; its means is the path of its course.

entries.pali: 703-705 . Tividhāyā ti kilesavatthuokāsavasena, kāmarāgakāmavitakkakāmāvacaradhammavasena vā tividhāya. Kilesakāmavasenā ti kilesakāmabhūtakāmadhātubhāvenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Adhippāyaṃ asallakkhento ti rūpadhātusahagatavasena anusetīti, rūpadhātudhammesu aññatarabhāvena rūpadhātupariyāpannoti ca pucchitabhāvaṃ asallakkhentoti attho.
entries.chinese_simplified: 703-705. ‘以三种’者，谓以烦恼、事、处所故；或以欲贪、欲寻、欲界法故，为三种。‘以烦恼欲故’者，谓以成烦恼欲之欲界的状态。‘不识其意趣’者，义谓不识所问之‘以与色界俱行而随眠’及‘以色界诸法中某一法的状态而系属于色界’之意。
entries.english: 'Threefold' means threefold by way of defilements, objects, and location; or threefold by way of sensual lust, sensual thought, and sense-sphere phenomena. 'By way of defilement-desire' means by way of being the sense-desire sphere which consists of defilement-desire. 'Not noting the intention' means that one has an underlying tendency associated with the form sphere; the meaning is that one does not note that the question is about being included in the form sphere by being one of the phenomena of the form sphere.

entries.pali: Gataṃ gamanaṃ pavattīti katvā vuttaṃ ‘‘gatamattaṃ gatimattaṃ gahaṇamatta’’ nti. Diṭṭhiyā hi gati pavatti evāti. Āsannakāraṇattā ti padaṭṭhānatāya, yonisomanasikāro viya hi kusalassa ayonisomanasikāro akusalassa accāsannahetu. Tathā hi satipi asaddhammasavanādikāraṇe ayoniso anāvajjite avavatthāpite ca natthi akusalappavatti. Tathā ca vakkhati aṭṭhakathāyaṃ ‘‘ayoniso akusala’’nti. Etena ekantakāraṇatā ca vuttatthā hoti. Paṭisaṅkhā sītādikhamanaṃ appamādavihāroti vuttaṃ ‘‘appamajjanaṃ khamana’’ nti. Tena satisaṃvaroti idha khantisaṃvaro vuttoti adhippāyo indriyasaṃvarassa vuttattā. Pahānasaṃvaro ti vīriyasaṃvaro . So hi ‘‘uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti pajahatī’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.26; a. ni. 4.14; 6.58) vuttoti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 作“已行、行、现行”解，故说“仅是已行、仅是行、仅是执取”。因为见之行即是现行。“因是近因”，即是作为近因。犹如如理作意是善法的（近因），不如理作意是不善法的极近因。的确，即使有听闻不正法等因，若不如理地不转向、不确立，则不善法不现行。义注中也将说：“不如理即不善”。由此，也说明了其为决定因。以省察忍受寒等，是不放逸住，故说“不放逸地忍受”。因此，此处说“念律仪”，其意是指“忍律仪”，因为已说了根律仪。“断律仪”即是“精进律仪”。因为它被说为：“对已生起的欲寻，不忍受、断除”等。
entries.english: Having taken 'gone' (gataṃ) to mean 'going' (gamanaṃ), that is, 'occurrence' (pavattī), it is said: 'mere going, mere movement, mere grasping.' For the movement (gati) of a view is indeed its occurrence (pavatti). 'Due to being a proximate cause' means by being a basis. For just as wise attention is for the wholesome, unwise attention is the most proximate cause for the unwholesome. Indeed, even when causes such as listening to the false Dhamma are present, if there is no unwise adverting and determining, there is no occurrence of the unwholesome. And so it will be said in the commentary: 'Unwisely, the unwholesome.' By this, its being the decisive cause is also expressed. Regarding 'heedfulness, endurance,' this means reflection, enduring cold and so forth, and dwelling with heedfulness. By this, the meaning is that here 'restraint by mindfulness' is spoken of as 'restraint by patience,' since 'restraint of the faculties' has already been mentioned. 'Restraint by abandoning' is restraint by effort. For that is spoken of in the passage beginning: 'One does not tolerate an arisen sensual thought, but abandons it...'

entries.pali: 703-705 . Kilesavatthuokāsavasenā ti kilesakāmavatthukāmabhūmivasena. Rūpadhātusahagatavasena anusetī ti kāmarāgo yathā kāmavitakkasaṅkhātāya kāmadhātuyā saha paccayasamavāye uppajjanāraho, tameva rūpadhātuyāpīti attho. Rāgādikāraṇalābhe uppattiarahatā hi anusayanaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 703-705. “以烦恼事和处所为依”是指以烦恼欲、事欲、欲界地为依。“与色界相应而潜伏”是说：欲贪，如同它能够在因缘聚合时与被称为欲寻的欲界(kāmadhātu)一同生起一样，在色界也同样如此，此即其义。因为随眠就是在获得贪等之因时具有生起的能力。
entries.english: 703-705. 'By way of the basis and location of defilements' means by way of sensual desire as a defilement, sensual objects as a basis, and the sensual-desire plane as a location. 'Lies latent accompanied by the form element' means: just as sensual lust is fit to arise in the sensual-desire element, designated as sensual thought, when there is a combination of conditions, so too is it in the form element. For an underlying tendency is the fitness to arise upon obtaining a cause such as lust and so on.

entries.work_title: 阿毗达摩入门古复注 Abhidhammāvatāra-Purāṇaṭīkā
entries.pali: 914-6 . Savipphārikabhāvenā ti yoniso saṅkappavasena kāmavitakkādiṃ madditvā pavattanato savipphārikasabhāvena. Nekkhammādipavattito ti ettha nekkhamma-ggahaṇena brahmavihāravajjaṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ gahitaṃ. Ādi -saddena tīsu brahmavihāresu paṭhamajjhānaṃ gahitanti vadanti. Avūpasantabhāvassā ti uddhaccassa sarūpakathanena taṃsahavattino anutāpasabhāvassa kukkuccassāpi sarūpaṃ kathitamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tathā sayañcevātisantato ti uddhaccapaṭipakkhasabhāvavacanena kukkuccapaṭipakkho pītibhāvopi. Tenāha ‘‘sukhaṃ uddhaccakukkuccadvayassā’’ ti. Matiyā anurūpattā ti paññāya anurūpattā. Tathā ca vuttaṃ ācariyadhammapāla ttherena ‘‘vicāro vicikicchāya paṭipakkho ārammaṇe anumajjanavasena paññāpatirūpakasabhāvattā’’ti. Potthakesu pana ‘‘pītiyā anurūpattā’’ti pāṭho dissati, tassa ca vicāro anumajjanasabhāvavantatāya pīti viya ārammaṇe anivattanto ogāhetvā pavattatīti pītiyā anurūpattā sandehasabhāvattā ārammaṇaṃ anajjhogāhetvā pavattamānāya vicikicchāya paṭipakkhoti atthaṃ vadanti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 所谓“以遍满的状态”，是由于通过如理作意，压制欲寻等而生起，故为遍满自性。“由出离等生起故”，此处以“出离”一词摄取除梵住外的初禅。有人说，以“等”字表示在三梵住中也摄取初禅。“未平息状态”者，当知，通过阐述掉举(uddhacca)的自性，与之俱行的、追悔自性的恶作(kukkucca)的自性也同样被说明了。同样，“自身亦极寂静”者，通过说掉举的对治自性，恶作的对治——喜的状态也被说明了。因此说：“乐是掉举与恶作二者的对治。”“与慧相应”者，即与智慧(paññā)相应。法护(Dhammapāla)长老亦如是说：“伺(vicāra)是疑(vicikicchā)的对治，因其于所缘有持续伺察的作用，具有与智慧相似的自性。”然而在诸经书中可见“与喜相应”的读法，其义为：伺具有持续伺察的自性，如喜一般沉入所缘而不退转地运作，故与喜相应；而疑具有犹豫的自性，无法沉入所缘而运作，故伺是疑的对治。
entries.english: 914–916. "Savipphārikabhāvena" means by having an expansive nature, because it proceeds by crushing sensual thoughts and the like through wise intention. "Nekkhammādipavattito": here, by the taking of "nekkhamma" (renunciation), the first jhāna, excluding the brahmavihāras, is taken. They say that by the word "ādi" (and so on), the first jhāna in the three brahmavihāras is taken. "Avūpasantabhāvassa": it should be understood that by describing the nature of restlessness, the nature of remorse, which has the nature of regret and accompanies it, is also described. Similarly, by "sayañcevātisantato" (being very tranquil by itself), with the word for the nature of the counterpart to restlessness, the counterpart to remorse—the state of joy—is also implied. Therefore it is said, "happiness is for the pair of restlessness and remorse." "Matiyā anurūpattā" means because of being in accordance with wisdom (paññā). And thus it was said by the Elder Ācariya Dhammapāla: "Investigation (vicāra) is the counterpart to doubt because it has the nature of a semblance of wisdom, by way of repeatedly examining the object." In some books, however, the reading "pītiyā anurūpattā" (being in accordance with joy) is seen. And they state its meaning thus: investigation, due to its nature of repeatedly examining, proceeds by plunging into the object without turning back, like joy; thus, being in accordance with joy, it is the counterpart to doubt, which, due to its nature of uncertainty, proceeds without fully plunging into the object.
